## Overview

This is a chart built around a quiet Life Palace and a very visible Body Palace. The Life Palace sits in the Yin 寅 branch and holds no main stars of its own; it borrows Tian Ji (the strategist, quick to plan and adjust) and Tai Yin (the gentle moon, sensitive and reflective) from the opposite Travel Palace. A person with an empty Life Palace tends to be a chameleon: the core self is shaped by circumstances, company and movement, and often blossoms more fully away from home or in changing settings. The bright, outward-facing part of the chart lives elsewhere.

The Body Palace, which shows where your energy actually goes and how you operate in later life, sits in the Spouse Palace, with Tian Liang (the elder, principled and protective) in brilliant brightness. Partnership, close one-to-one commitments and the home you build with someone else are central to how you spend yourself. The Five Element Bureau is Earth 5, a steady, grounded frame that gives this airy, adaptable Life Palace a practical anchor.

The most distinctive traits are adaptability (Tian Ji and Tai Yin borrowed into an empty Life Palace) and outward generosity (Tai Yang, the sun, bright and carrying birth-year Hua Lu, prosperity, in the Career Palace). You are likely to be better at showing up for others and for the work than at asserting a fixed personal identity, so building routines that anchor you pays off.

## Life Palace and Personality

The Life Palace in Yin 寅 is empty, borrowing Tian Ji (steady) and Tai Yin (fair) from the Travel Palace. Tian Ji is the quick, analytical planner who reads a room and shifts course; Tai Yin is the soft, intuitive moon, attentive to mood and beauty. Together they describe someone who thinks fast, feels deeply and adapts well, but who may feel unsure of the "real" self when there is too little external structure. Supporting stars here: none, so the personality is uncluttered and driven mostly by these two borrowed qualities.

An empty Life Palace also means the opposite palace matters greatly. Your Travel Palace holds the same stars, one of which — Tai Yin — carries birth-year Hua Ke (recognition). Travel, study, and unfamiliar settings tend to bring out your best and earn you quiet respect. Working with this tendency means deliberately putting yourself in new environments rather than staying in one fixed place.

The inner life has its own texture: the Spirit Palace (inner contentment and mindset, not the Health Palace) holds Tian Tong (the easygoing, pleasure-seeking star) with birth-year Hua Ji (obstacle, needs extra care) and the challenging Di Jie. Tian Tong here suggests you find contentment easily but can drift into comfort; with Hua Ji and Di Jie, emotional satisfaction is something you have to work at consciously rather than expect to arrive. Notice when you are soothing yourself rather than solving something, and give the mind real challenges.

## Career

The Career Palace in Wu 午 holds Tai Yang (the sun: visibility, generosity, leadership) in bright strength and with birth-year Hua Lu (prosperity), plus the challenging Di Kong (the void star, which can make effort feel abstract). This is the strongest single placement in the chart: work that puts you in front of people — teaching, client-facing roles, leadership, communications, service — suits you and tends to bring material reward. Hua Lu on Tai Yang points to reputation translating into livelihood.

Di Kong in this palace is the counterweight. It can pull toward work that feels ungrounded, or toward a sense of effort not turning into visible results. Channel it by pairing your visible role with something concrete and measurable — a craft, a physical product, a clear metric you track — so the sun has something solid to shine on. The Career Palace is also the current Major Period palace, so these themes are at their most active now.

## Wealth

The Wealth Palace in Xu 戌 holds Ju Men (the debater, the talker, the negotiator) in fallen brightness, and its opposite Spirit Palace holds Tian Tong (neutral). Ju Men in a fallen state suggests money that comes through speech, persuasion, contracts and information, but with a tendency to overcomplicate, argue, or talk yourself into and out of opportunities. It is not a palace of easy passive gain; it rewards skill in words and negotiation, and punishes carelessness with detail.

The Property Palace in Si 巳 holds Wu Qu (the general: discipline, execution) with birth-year Hua Quan (power), plus Po Jun (the pioneer who clears the old to build the new), and the auspicious You Bi and Wen Chang. This is a strong property and asset signature: Hua Quan on Wu Qu gives you the drive and authority to acquire and hold tangible things, while Po Jun warns that you may rebuild more than once. Wen Chang here supports careful documentation and planning.

Work with the wealth picture by treating talking as a professional skill — prepare, negotiate, document — and by letting Wu Qu's discipline, not Ju Men's cleverness, govern your long-term decisions. The August support stars in the Property Palace are best used through methodical budgeting and clear records rather than impulse.

## Love and Partnership

The Spouse Palace in Zi 子 holds Tian Liang (the elder, principled and protective) in brilliant brightness and is also where the Body Palace sits; its opposite Career Palace holds Tai Yang (bright) with Hua Lu. This is a warm, stable signature: a partner or relationship that feels responsible, mature and sheltering, and that connects closely to your work and public life. With the Body Palace here, you are most yourself in a committed partnership, not in solitary ambition.

There are no challenging stars in the Spouse Palace, which is a clean, supportive placement; the main work is that Tian Liang can be a little paternalistic — you may expect your partner to guide or protect you, or you may play that role for them. Keep the relationship mutual rather than casting it into parent and child.

The Children Palace in Hai 亥 holds Tian Xiang (the steady minister: loyal, procedural) and its opposite Property Palace carries Wu Qu and Po Jun, so family-building tends to be orderly and practical. Treatings partnership as a shared project with clear roles suits you, but leave room for spontaneity.

## Wellbeing Habits

The Health Palace in You 酉 holds Zi Wei (the emperor: dignity, centrality) in bright strength and Tan Lang (the sensualist: desire, appetite, sociability), supported by Zuo Fu, Wen Qu and the challenging Qing Yang. Zi Wei suggests you handle strain best when you feel in control and respected; Tan Lang points to appetite — food, drink, pleasure — as the place where habits are most likely to slip. Qing Yang is a sharp, friction-making star that can drive you to push through tiredness rather than rest, so pace yourself consciously.

For sleep, the bright Zi Wei favours a settled evening routine that feels dignified and calm; Tan Lang may tempt you to keep the evening going, so a clear wind-down helps. For food, Tan Lang's love of pleasure is best given quality over quantity. For movement, Qing Yang and Zi Wei together suit structured, deliberate exercise with clear goals, and Wen Qu suggests learning-based movement (a skill, a practice) keeps you engaged. For emotional balance, the Spirit Palace's Tian Tong with Hua Ji and Di Jie means contentment needs active cultivation; the borrowed Tai Yin in the Life Palace makes reflective time, music and quiet genuinely restorative.

If you feel unwell, please consult a qualified healthcare professional.

## Family and Social Circle

The Parents Palace in Mao 卯 is empty, borrowing Zi Wei (bright) and Tan Lang (fair) from the Health Palace, and holds the challenging Ling Xing. Parents or authority figures may loom large and be demanding of your dignity, with Ling Xing adding a brisk, sometimes impatient edge to those relationships. The borrowed emperor star suggests you look to elders for a sense of legitimacy; the lesson is to claim your own authority rather than waiting for approval.

The Friends Palace in Wei 未 holds Tian Fu (the treasurer: steady, resourceful, dependable) in brilliant brightness, with Tian Yue (auspicious) plus the challenging Tuo Luo and Huo Xing. Tian Fu and Tian Yue make your wider circle genuinely supportive and steady. Tuo Luo and Huo Xing bring slow friction and quick flare-ups — a friend group that occasionally tests your patience or runs hot. Channel that energy through shared activity or competition rather than argument.

The Siblings Palace in Chou 丑 holds Lian Zhen (fair, a sharp and sometimes severe star) and Qi Sha (brilliant, the disciplined fighter), with Tian Kui (auspicious). Siblings or close peers can be intense and competitive, but Tian Kui brings a helpful ally among them. The Children Palace's Tian Xiang suggests steadiness and loyalty in the next generation and in your relationship with younger people.

## Major Period and Year by Year

The Current Major Period runs through the Career Palace in Wu 午, ages 45–54 (about 2024–2033), built on Tai Yang (bright) with birth-year Hua Lu. These ten years put visibility, reputation and career in the foreground: work is the arena where effort turns into reward, and staying visible matters more than staying safe. The pace is outward and public, so guard energy and let Di Kong's void feeling be met with concrete milestones. The Next Major Period moves to the Friends Palace in Wei 未 from ages 55–64 (about 2034–2043), centred on Tian Fu (brilliant) — a shift toward community, networks and steady resource-building, with the challenging Tuo Luo and Huo Xing requiring patience in group settings.

Each annual pillar below follows the Chinese lunar year and roughly matches the calendar year.

### 2026 丙午 · Bing Wu

The annual Life Palace for 2026 falls on your Career Palace with Tai Yang (bright), so the year's tone is public, professional and outward-facing, doubling the emphasis of the current Major Period. Hua Lu lands on Tian Tong in the natal Spirit Palace — contentment and ease are worth leaning into, and small pleasures restore you. Hua Quan goes to Tian Ji in the natal Travel Palace, giving momentum to travel or study; Hua Ke goes to Wen Chang in the natal Property Palace, favouring careful documentation and planning. Hua Ji goes to Lian Zhen in the natal Siblings Palace, so peer and sibling matters call for more care and a slower pace — avoid unnecessary friction there.

### 2027 丁未 · Ding Wei

The Friends Palace with Tian Fu (brilliant) becomes the annual Life Palace, turning attention to networks, groups and steady allies. Hua Lu lands on Tai Yin in the natal Travel Palace, which is a good time to travel, study or work at a distance. Hua Quan goes to Tian Tong in the natal Spirit Palace, giving inner contentment a productive push; Hua Ke goes to Tian Ji in the natal Travel Palace, adding recognition to planning and movement. Hua Ji falls on Ju Men in the natal Wealth Palace, so money matters deserve extra care and clear communication — keep contracts and conversations precise.

### 2028 戊申 · Wu Shen

The Travel Palace with Tian Ji (steady) and Tai Yin (fair) becomes the annual Life Palace, making this a year of movement, adaption and reflection. Hua Lu lands on Tan Lang in the natal Health Palace, a good time to put energy into physical wellbeing and enjoyment in moderation. Hua Quan goes to Tai Yin in the natal Travel Palace, giving quiet influence through travel and study; Hua Ke goes to You Bi in the natal Property Palace, supporting practical asset decisions made with care. Hua Ji also falls on Tian Ji in the natal Travel Palace, so plans that involve moving or changing direction call for a slower pace and a backup plan.

### 2029 己酉 · Ji You

The Health Palace with Zi Wei (bright) and Tan Lang (fair) becomes the annual Life Palace, turning the year inward toward health, dignity and self-mastery. Hua Lu lands on Wu Qu in the natal Property Palace, favouring methodical, disciplined progress on long-term assets. Hua Quan goes to Tan Lang in the natal Health Palace, giving appetite and drive a productive outlet; Hua Ke goes to Tian Liang in the natal Spouse Palace, bringing warmth and recognition to partnership. Hua Ji falls on Wen Qu in the natal Health Palace, so the pace of study and self-discipline needs adjusting — build in rest rather than pushing through.

### 2030 庚戌 · Geng Xu

The Wealth Palace with Ju Men (fallen) becomes the annual Life Palace, so money, speech and negotiation are the year's theme; lean into your persuasive skill but keep detail rigorous. Hua Lu lands on Tai Yang in the natal Career Palace, which is a strong year to seek visibility and reward at work. Hua Quan goes to Wu Qu in the natal Property Palace, adding authority to asset decisions; Hua Ke goes to Tai Yin in the natal Travel Palace, bringing quiet recognition through movement or learning. Hua Ji falls on Tian Tong in the natal Spirit Palace, so emotional contentment deserves care — guard rest and avoid soothing yourself into avoidance.

## Guidance

- Put yourself in new settings deliberately, since the Life Palace is empty and borrows Tian Ji and Tai Yin from the Travel Palace: a course, a trip, or a change of scene tends to bring out your best.
- Pair your public role (Tai Yang with Hua Lu in the Career Palace) with a concrete, measurable craft or metric, so the challenging Di Kong in the same palace does not leave effort feeling abstract.
- Treat negotiation and clear documentation as a professional skill, given Ju Men (fallen) in the Wealth Palace and Wen Chang in the Property Palace: prepare and record rather than improvise.
- Pace yourself physically using the Health Palace's Tan Lang and Qing Yang: fixed wind-down times, quality over quantity in food, and structured movement rather than pushing through tiredness.
- In the current Career Palace Major Period, choose visible milestones each season; when the Next Major Period brings Tian Fu in the Friends Palace, shift attention toward community and networks.
